title: Coinbase insider breach: bribed support agents leaked customer data, feeding a 'safe wallet' impersonation-call wave
summary: Criminals bribed overseas Coinbase support agents to copy customer data — names, contacts, last-4 SSNs, ID images, balances — then demanded $20M on May 11, 2025. Coinbase refused (SEC 8-K + Coinbase blog, May 15). No passwords, keys, or funds taken. The leaked data fuels ongoing impersonation calls pushing users to a 'safe' wallet; Coinbase pledged to reimburse customers tricked before May 15.

impact.lossNative: $307M in expenses related to the data theft incident, booked in Q2 2025 per Coinbase's shareholder letter (SEC EDGAR, filed July 31, 2025) — Coinbase's own costs, superseding the preliminary $180M–$400M estimate in the May 15 8-K. Victim losses to the follow-on impersonation calls are not separately totaled by any primary source.
impact.victims: 69,461 customers per Coinbase's breach notice to the Maine Attorney General (as reported); 'less than 1% of Coinbase monthly transacting users' per Coinbase

timeline.event: Unauthorized copying of customer data by overseas support agents begins, per Coinbase's later breach notice to the Maine Attorney General (as reported — see claims; the notice itself could not be fetched directly).

Coinbase security monitoring independently detects support personnel accessing customer data without business need. The personnel are terminated immediately, fraud-monitoring protections heightened, and customers whose information was potentially accessed are warned.

Coinbase receives an extortion email from an unknown threat actor demanding money in exchange for not publicly disclosing stolen customer-account data and internal documentation. Coinbase assesses the email as credible and concludes the earlier improper accesses were a single campaign that succeeded in taking data from internal systems.

Coinbase files Form 8-K under Item 1.05 (Material Cybersecurity Incident, event date May 14) and publishes 'Protecting Our Customers — Standing Up to Extortionists': it refuses the $20M ransom, establishes a $20M reward fund for information leading to arrest and conviction, pledges to voluntarily reimburse tricked retail customers, and begins opening a US support hub. Notification emails to affected customers go out at 7:20 a.m. ET from no-reply@info.coinbase.com.

Coinbase's breach notice filed with the Maine Attorney General reportedly puts the affected count at 69,461 customers nationwide and dates the breach start to December 26, 2024; affected users are offered credit monitoring.
Coinbase's June update reportedly ties the bribed agents to the India operations of outsourcing firm TaskUs; TaskUs shuts down the involved department.

Coinbase's Q2 2025 shareholder letter, filed as an 8-K exhibit on SEC EDGAR, reports total operating expenses driven up by $307 million in expenses related to the data theft incident disclosed in May.

Brooklyn DA announces a 31-count indictment of Ronald Spektor, 23, for allegedly impersonating Coinbase representatives and stealing nearly $16M from about 100 users nationwide by warning them their assets were 'at risk' and moving them to attacker-controlled wallets. The DA release does not link the scheme to this breach — it is the same impersonation playbook the leaked data enables. Allegations, not findings.

Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong announces the first arrest in India tied to the insider breach — a former support agent arrested in Hyderabad; more arrests expected. (Date is the announcement; the arrest itself may predate it.)

affected: ~69,461 Coinbase retail customers whose records were copied (per Coinbase's Maine AG notice, as reported). Coinbase notified this group by email from no-reply@info.coinbase.com at 7:20 a.m. ET on May 15, 2025

Data taken (per the 8-K): name, address, phone, email; masked SSN (last 4 digits only); masked bank-account numbers and some identifiers; government-ID images (driver's license, passport); balance snapshots and transaction history; limited internal corporate data
Every Coinbase user is a target of the follow-on impersonation calls and texts — the script works with or without your leaked record
notAffected: Passwords, 2FA codes, and private keys — not compromised (Coinbase 8-K and blog)
Customer funds — the bribed agents had no ability to access or move funds
Customers who did not receive the May 15, 2025 notice from no-reply@info.coinbase.com were not in the affected data set, per Coinbase
actions: Hang up on any call or text claiming to be Coinbase. Coinbase states it will never call to move your funds to a 'safe' wallet, give you a seed phrase or deposit address, ask for your password or 2FA codes, or tell you to call a number. The call itself is the scam — there is no account emergency.
Mid-conversation or already acted? Lock your account in the Coinbase app right now, then email security@coinbase.com. Minutes matter more than embarrassment.

If you sent funds to the attackers as a direct result of this incident, Coinbase committed in its SEC 8-K and blog to voluntarily reimburse eligible retail customers after review. Coinbase's stated criteria cover retail customers who mistakenly sent funds before the May 15, 2025 disclosure; if you were tricked later, still report it via coinbase.com support — but do not assume reimbursement. Pursue this only through coinbase.com or in-app support — never through anyone who contacts you first, and never through a third-party 'claims agent'.

Report the contact to the FBI at ic3.gov, and handle identity-theft fallout at identitytheft.gov. Your ID images and last-4 SSN outlive the news cycle: freeze your credit with all three bureaus and set a port-out/SIM-swap PIN with your mobile carrier.
Harden the account today: switch 2FA to a hardware security key and enable withdrawal allow-listing so funds can only move to wallets you already control.
Ignore anyone offering to recover crypto lost to this scam for a fee — recovery pitches are the second half of the same scam. Only law enforcement can seize and return funds.

claims.claim: The threat actor obtained the data by paying multiple contractors or employees in overseas support roles to collect information from internal Coinbase systems; the May 11, 2025 email demanded money ($20M per Coinbase's blog), which Coinbase refused while cooperating with law enforcement.

Preliminary expense estimate of approximately $180M–$400M for remediation and voluntary customer reimbursements, 'prior to further review of potential losses, indemnification claims, and potential recoveries'.
69,461 customers were affected and the unauthorized access began December 26, 2024, per Coinbase's data-breach notice filed with the Maine Attorney General.
claims.attribution: Maine AG filing as reported by The Block and SecurityWeek; the Maine AG notice page could not be fetched directly for verification

claims.claim: The bribed agents worked at outsourcing firm TaskUs' India operations; TaskUs shut down the involved department, and a former support agent was arrested in Hyderabad in December 2025 with more arrests expected per CEO Brian Armstrong.
claims.attribution: Coinbase June 2025 update and Indian police, as reported by BleepingComputer and The Block; no official Indian charging document fetched

claims.claim: The Brooklyn DA alleges Ronald Spektor, 23, of Sheepshead Bay stole nearly $16M from about 100 Coinbase users via an impersonation phishing scheme (31-count indictment: grand larceny, money laundering, scheme to defraud; ~$105K cash and ~$400K crypto seized). These are allegations; no court has ruled on them as of 2026-08-11, and the DA does not connect the scheme to the insider breach.
claims.attribution: Brooklyn District Attorney's Office press release, December 19, 2025
